title: Does the factory catalogue count as seeing the part
ask: Does a part the factory catalogue lists for this car, on a system nothing has changed, count as a fact about the car now without you looking at it?
why: The Manual (D-417) shows a part only when nothing about it says confirm. 237 parts are held today for that word alone, and for about 182 of them the doubt is not a measurement but 'is this internal factory part still fitted?' - an oil pan, an eccentric shaft, a brush holder - written by the catalogue transcription because nobody has looked. Each became one of your 290 verify rows ('Is the Oil pan (PT077) on the car as described?'), most of them about parts you cannot see without taking something apart. Meanwhile the Manual hides 28 % of the parts list. Whether a part the factory catalogue lists for this chassis (fits=yes), on a system nothing has changed, counts as a fact about your car without you looking at it is your bar (your spec answer 4.5), not the agent's; it decides how many of the 290 taps exist.
options:
(a) Yes: a fits=yes catalogue row on a system nothing has changed is backed. 'confirm' stays only where a known change touches the system (the carburettor and air cleaner, emissions, the removed metering pump, the optional equipment you have already ruled on) or the scan was unreadable. The B-K rows for the rest are dropped - roughly 200 fewer taps - and the Manual shows those parts marked 'from the factory catalogue, not yet seen'.
(b) No: every part is seen before it is shown. The 290 rows stay (at a minute a row, about five hours of tapping across several sessions), and the Manual fills in as you go.
(c) Yes for what cannot be seen without disassembly (inside the engine, gearbox, axles, doors); no for what is visible from the driveway or under the hood, which stays on your list. Roughly halves the list.
recommend: (a), unless you want the Manual to show only what you have personally seen - then (c).
stops: Plan step P29 (collapsing the verify list) and how many of the 290 rows remain.
